requirements.requirement: Configure node1 so the running kernel boots with audit=1.
requirements.summary: After the reboot, /proc/cmdline contained audit=1 and kernel messages directly reported auditing enabled and initialized.

The GRUB Legacy kopt template and generated kernel entries contained audit=1, and a bounded reboot produced a different boot ID with audit=1 still present in both the live command line and persistent configuration.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use a legacy-compatible implementation.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 7.10 and continued running kernel 2.6.22-14-generic after reboot. The executor used the platform's existing GRUB Legacy menu.lst and update-grub mechanism without installing or replacing software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre/post evidence shows a genuine reboot, recovery, unchanged legacy OS/kernel, persistent GRUB configuration, and a live kernel with auditing initialized.
limitations: The restart protocol directly established baseline health, restart scheduling, an intervening SSH outage, changed boot identity, writable-root recovery, and recovered task state. It did not separately probe application-service, workload-data, or cluster state; none was identified in this single-node task.

Failed-service collection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, so absence of failed services could not be independently assessed (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services).
auditctl was not installed, so audit activation was verified through the live kernel command line and kernel boot messages rather than auditctl status (cmd-eda2dd26bf674b76, cmd-951f3fd5591c4ef4).

operational_hygiene.summary: The required configuration and reboot were narrowly scoped, package health and listening-socket observations remained unchanged, and no temporary-file residue remained. One low-risk unnecessary mutation occurred: the apparent update-grub version probe actually regenerated menu.lst before the intended edit. That premature regeneration was superfluous; no distinct residue was observed, and the file was subsequently regenerated with the required configuration. The safety backup and reboot log were task-related and absent from the final /tmp inventory.
